subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that pauses or aborts active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or keep supported steering boundary-based?
rationale: The choice affects core agent lifecycle semantics, channel delivery guarantees, Codex/native runtime integration, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt queue modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume behavior with tests and docs for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer behavior as the supported default and limit follow-up work to ensuring messages reach the existing boundary-based queue policy.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainer-approved upgrade proof across channels and runtimes.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume behavior with tests and docs for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They are connected to the prior maintainer replacement PR for active non-streaming steering and are a strong owner for the shared queue/runtime tradeoff.
